title: Bhajagovindam (Mohamudgara)
subtitle: Thirty-one verses of instruction and devotion

source.digitalText: Sanskrit transcription; lexical word meanings consulted for cross-check
source.crossCheck: Common 31-verse recension; later appended verses excluded
source.changes: Replaced generic ranges with four descriptive contents links: the opening verse, the traditional Dvādaśamañjarikā (verses 2–13), the Caturdaśamañjarikā (verses 14–27), and the closing verses (28–31). Audited every verse’s Sanskrit, explicit IAST, English translation, and Devanāgarī word gloss against the cited 31-verse recension.

translationCredit: Original English translation and word-for-word gloss.

units.label: Verse 1
units.deva:
भज गोविन्दं भज गोविन्दं
गोविन्दं भज मूढमते ।
सम्प्राप्ते सन्निहिते काले
नहि नहि रक्षति डुकृङ्करणे ॥ १॥
units.translation: Worship Govinda, worship Govinda; worship Govinda, O foolish mind! When the appointed time has arrived and is close at hand, no, no—the ḍukṛñkaraṇa grammar formula will not protect you.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
bhaja govindaṃ bhaja govindaṃ
govindaṃ bhaja mūḍhamate |
samprāpte sannihite kāle
nahi nahi rakṣati ḍukṛṅkaraṇe || 1||

units.label: Verse 2
units.deva:
मूढ जहीहि धनागमतृष्णां
कुरु सद्बुद्धिं मनसि वितृष्णाम् ।
यल्लभसे निजकर्मोपात्तं
वित्तं तेन विनोदय चित्तम् ॥ २॥
units.translation: Fool, abandon the thirst for acquiring wealth. Cultivate good understanding and freedom from craving in your mind. Whatever wealth you gain through your own actions, use it to make your mind content.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
mūḍha jahīhi dhanāgamatṛṣṇāṃ
kuru sadbuddhiṃ manasi vitṛṣṇām |
yallabhase nijakarmopāttaṃ
vittaṃ tena vinodaya cittam || 2||

units.label: Verse 3
units.deva:
नारीस्तनभरनाभीदेशं
दृष्ट्वा मा गा मोहावेशम् ।
एतन्मांसवसादिविकारं
मनसि विचिन्तय वारं वारम् ॥ ३॥
units.translation: On seeing a woman’s breasts and navel region, do not fall under the spell of delusion. Reflect again and again in the mind: this is a transformation of flesh, fat, and the like.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
nārīstanabharanābhīdeśaṃ
dṛṣṭvā mā gā mohāveśam |
etanmāṃsavasādivikāraṃ
manasi vicintaya vāraṃ vāram || 3||

units.label: Verse 4
units.deva:
नलिनीदलगतजलमतितरलं
तद्वज्जीवितमतिशयचपलम् ।
विद्धि व्याध्यभिमानग्रस्तं
लोकं शोकहतं च समस्तम् ॥ ४॥
units.translation: Water lying on a lotus leaf is very unstable; so too is life exceedingly fragile. Know that the entire world is seized by disease and conceit, and struck by sorrow.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
nalinīdalagatajalamatitaralaṃ
tadvajjīvitamatiśayacapalam |
viddhi vyādhyabhimānagrastaṃ
lokaṃ śokahataṃ ca samastam || 4||

units.label: Verse 5
units.deva:
यावद्वित्तोपार्जनसक्त-
स्तावन्निजपरिवारो रक्तः ।
पश्चाज्जीवति जर्जरदेहे
वार्तां कोऽपि न पृच्छति गेहे ॥ ५॥
units.translation: So long as you are intent on earning wealth, your own family is attached to you. Later, when you live on in a worn-out body, no one at home asks after you.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
yāvadvittopārjanasakta-
stāvannijaparivāro raktaḥ |
paścājjīvati jarjaradehe
vārtāṃ ko’pi na pṛcchati gehe || 5||

units.label: Verse 6
units.deva:
यावत्पवनो निवसति देहे
तावत्पृच्छति कुशलं गेहे ।
गतवति वायौ देहापाये
भार्या बिभ्यति तस्मिन्काये ॥ ६॥
units.translation: As long as breath dwells in the body, those at home ask about your welfare. When the breath has gone and the body has fallen, the wife fears that body.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
yāvatpavano nivasati dehe
tāvatpṛcchati kuśalaṃ gehe |
gatavati vāyau dehāpāye
bhāryā bibhyati tasminkāye || 6||

units.label: Verse 7
units.deva:
बालस्तावत्क्रीडासक्तः
तरुणस्तावत्तरुणीसक्तः ।
वृद्धस्तावच्चिन्तासक्तः
परमे ब्रह्मणि कोऽपि न सक्तः ॥ ७॥
units.translation: A child is absorbed in play; a young person is absorbed in a young woman; an old person is absorbed in worry. No one, it seems, is absorbed in supreme Brahman.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
bālastāvatkrīḍāsaktaḥ
taruṇastāvattaruṇīsaktaḥ |
vṛddhastāvaccintāsaktaḥ
parame brahmaṇi ko’pi na saktaḥ || 7||

units.label: Verse 8
units.deva:
का ते कान्ता कस्ते पुत्रः
संसारोऽयमतीव विचित्रः ।
कस्य त्वं कः कुत आयात-
स्तत्त्वं चिन्तय तदिह भ्रातः ॥ ८॥
units.translation: Who is your wife? Who is your son? This worldly life is so strange. Who do you belong to? Who are you? From where have you come? Brother, reflect on the truth here.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
kā te kāntā kaste putraḥ
saṃsāro’yamatīva vicitraḥ |
kasya tvaṃ kaḥ kuta āyāta-
stattvaṃ cintaya tadiha bhrātaḥ || 8||

units.label: Verse 9
units.deva:
सत्सङ्गत्वे निस्सङ्गत्वं
निस्सङ्गत्वे निर्मोहत्वम् ।
निर्मोहत्वे निश्चलतत्त्वं
निश्चलतत्त्वे जीवन्मुक्तिः ॥ ९॥
units.translation: From association with the good comes nonattachment; from nonattachment, freedom from delusion; from freedom from delusion, steadiness in truth; from steadiness in truth, liberation while living.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
satsaṅgatve nissaṅgatvaṃ
nissaṅgatve nirmohatvam |
nirmohatve niścalatattvaṃ
niścalatattve jīvanmuktiḥ || 9||

units.label: Verse 10
units.deva:
वयसि गते कः कामविकारः
शुष्के नीरे कः कासारः ।
क्षीणे वित्ते कः परिवारः
ज्ञाते तत्त्वे कः संसारः ॥ १०॥
units.translation: When youth has passed, what sexual desire remains? When the water is dry, what lake remains? When wealth is depleted, what family remains? When truth is known, what worldly existence remains?
units.sectionTitle: Verses 1–10 · Impermanence, worldly attachments, and good company
units.iast:
vayasi gate kaḥ kāmavikāraḥ
śuṣke nīre kaḥ kāsāraḥ |
kṣīṇe vitte kaḥ parivāraḥ
jñāte tattve kaḥ saṃsāraḥ || 10||

units.label: Verse 11
units.deva:
मा कुरु धनजनयौवनगर्वं
हरति निमेषात्कालः सर्वम् ।
मायामयमिदमखिलं हित्वा
ब्रह्मपदं त्वं प्रविश विदित्वा ॥ ११॥
units.translation: Do not be proud of wealth, family, or youth; time takes it all away in an instant. Leave behind this whole thing made of māyā; knowing the state of Brahman, enter it.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
mā kuru dhanajanayauvanagarvaṃ
harati nimeṣātkālaḥ sarvam |
māyāmayamidamakhilaṃ hitvā
brahmapadaṃ tvaṃ praviśa viditvā || 11||

units.label: Verse 12
units.deva:
दिनयामिन्यौ सायं प्रातः
शिशिरवसन्तौ पुनरायातः ।
कालः क्रीडति गच्छत्यायु-
स्तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशावायुः ॥ १२॥
units.translation: Day and night, evening and morning, winter and spring come around again. Time plays on and life passes; even then, the wind of desire does not let go.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
dinayāminyau sāyaṃ prātaḥ
śiśiravasantau punarāyātaḥ |
kālaḥ krīḍati gacchatyāyu-
stadapi na muñcatyāśāvāyuḥ || 12||

units.label: Verse 13
units.deva:
का ते कान्ता धनगतचिन्ता
वातुल किं तव नास्ति नियन्ता ।
त्रिजगति सज्जनसङ्गतिरेका
भवति भवार्णवतरणे नौका ॥ १३॥
units.translation: What is your beloved, what is your worry about wealth? O restless one, do you have no guide? In the three worlds, the company of good people alone becomes the boat for crossing the ocean of worldly existence.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
kā te kāntā dhanagatacintā
vātula kiṃ tava nāsti niyantā |
trijagati sajjanasaṅgatirekā
bhavati bhavārṇavataraṇe naukā || 13||

units.label: Verse 14
units.deva:
जटिलो मुण्डी लुञ्छितकेशः
काषायाम्बरबहुकृतवेषः ।
पश्यन्नपि च न पश्यति मूढो
ह्युदरनिमित्तं बहुकृतवेषः ॥ १४॥
units.translation: One has matted hair, another a shaved head, another hair plucked out; wearing ochre garments, one adopts many guises. Though he sees, the deluded one does not see; he takes on many guises for the sake of his belly.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
jaṭilo muṇḍī luñchitakeśaḥ
kāṣāyāmbarabahukṛtaveṣaḥ |
paśyannapi ca na paśyati mūḍho
hyudaranimittaṃ bahukṛtaveṣaḥ || 14||

units.label: Verse 15
units.deva:
अङ्गं गलितं पलितं मुण्डं
दशनविहीनं जातं तुण्डम् ।
वृद्धो याति गृहीत्वा दण्डं
तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशापिण्डम् ॥ १५॥
units.translation: The body has withered, the hair turned gray, the head become bald, and the mouth become toothless. An old person walks holding a staff, yet still does not abandon the bundle of hopes.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
aṅgaṃ galitaṃ palitaṃ muṇḍaṃ
daśanavihīnaṃ jātaṃ tuṇḍam |
vṛddho yāti gṛhītvā daṇḍaṃ
tadapi na muñcatyāśāpiṇḍam || 15||

units.label: Verse 16
units.deva:
अग्रे वह्निः पृष्ठे भानुः
रात्रौ चुबुकसमर्पितजानुः ।
करतलभिक्षस्तरुतलवास-
स्तदपि न मुञ्चत्याशापाशः ॥ १६॥
units.translation: Fire in front, sun behind; at night the knees drawn up to the chin; alms in the palm, dwelling beneath a tree—yet even then the noose of desire does not let go.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
agre vahniḥ pṛṣṭhe bhānuḥ
rātrau cubukasamarpitajānuḥ |
karatalabhikṣastarutalavāsa-
stadapi na muñcatyāśāpāśaḥ || 16||

units.label: Verse 17
units.deva:
कुरुते गङ्गासागरगमनं
व्रतपरिपालनमथवा दानम् ।
ज्ञानविहीनः सर्वमतेन
मुक्तिं न भजति जन्मशतेन ॥ १७॥
units.translation: One may make the pilgrimage to Gaṅgāsāgara, keep vows, or give alms. But, lacking knowledge, one does not attain liberation even in a hundred births, by any account.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
kurute gaṅgāsāgaragamanaṃ
vrataparipālanamathavā dānam |
jñānavihīnaḥ sarvamatena
muktiṃ na bhajati janmaśatena || 17||

units.label: Verse 18
units.deva:
सुरमंदिरतरुमूलनिवासः
शय्या भूतलमजिनं वासः ।
सर्वपरिग्रहभोगत्यागः
कस्य सुखं न करोति विरागः ॥ १८॥
units.translation: Dwelling in a temple or at the foot of a tree, the earth for a bed and a deerskin for clothing, giving up all possessions and pleasures—what happiness does dispassion not bring?
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
suramaṃdiratarumūlanivāsaḥ
śayyā bhūtalamajinaṃ vāsaḥ |
sarvaparigrahabhogatyāgaḥ
kasya sukhaṃ na karoti virāgaḥ || 18||

units.label: Verse 19
units.deva:
योगरतो वा भोगरतो वा
सङ्गरतो वा सङ्गविहीनः ।
यस्य ब्रह्मणि रमते चित्तं
नन्दति नन्दति नन्दत्येव ॥ १९॥
units.translation: Whether delighting in yoga or in pleasure, attached or free from attachment, the one whose mind delights in Brahman rejoices, rejoices, indeed rejoices.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
yogarato vā bhogarato vā
saṅgarato vā saṅgavihīnaḥ |
yasya brahmaṇi ramate cittaṃ
nandati nandati nandatyeva || 19||

units.label: Verse 20
units.deva:
भगवद्गीता किञ्चिदधीता
गङ्गाजललवकणिका पीता ।
सकृदपि येन मुरारिसमर्चा
क्रियते तस्य यमेन न चर्चा ॥ २०॥
units.translation: Whoever studies even a little of the Bhagavad Gītā, drinks a tiny drop of Ganges water, and worships Murāri even once has no discussion with Yama.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 11–20 · Dispassion, knowledge, and disciplined practice
units.iast:
bhagavadgītā kiñcidadhītā
gaṅgājalalavakaṇikā pītā |
sakṛdapi yena murārisamarcā
kriyate tasya yamena na carcā || 20||

units.label: Verse 21
units.deva:
पुनरपि जननं पुनरपि मरणं
पुनरपि जननीजठरे शयनम् ।
इह संसारे बहुदुस्तारे
कृपयाऽपारे पाहि मुरारे ॥ २१॥
units.translation: Birth again, death again, lying again in the mother’s womb! In this worldly existence, so hard to cross, protect me by your boundless compassion, O Murāri.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
punarapi jananaṃ punarapi maraṇaṃ
punarapi jananījaṭhare śayanam |
iha saṃsāre bahudustāre
kṛpayā’pāre pāhi murāre || 21||

units.label: Verse 22
units.deva:
रथ्याचर्पटविरचितकन्थः
पुण्यापुण्यविवर्जितपन्थः ।
योगी योगनियोजितचित्तो
रमते बालोन्मत्तवदेव ॥ २२॥
units.translation: The yogin wears a garment stitched from rags found on the road and walks a path free from merit and demerit; with the mind focused on yoga, that yogin delights just like a child or a mad person.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
rathyācarpaṭaviracitakanthaḥ
puṇyāpuṇyavivarjitapanthaḥ |
yogī yoganiyojitacitto
ramate bālonmattavadeva || 22||

units.label: Verse 23
units.deva:
कस्त्वं कोऽहं कुत आयातः
का मे जननी को मे तातः ।
इति परिभावय सर्वमसारम्
विश्वं त्यक्त्वा स्वप्नविचारम् ॥ २३॥
units.translation: Who are you? Who am I? From where have I come? Who is my mother? Who is my father? Reflect on this: the whole world is without essence. Leave it behind and regard it as a dream.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
kastvaṃ ko’haṃ kuta āyātaḥ
kā me jananī ko me tātaḥ |
iti paribhāvaya sarvamasāram
viśvaṃ tyaktvā svapnavicāram || 23||

units.label: Verse 24
units.deva:
त्वयि मयि चान्यत्रैको विष्णु-
र्व्यर्थं कुप्यसि मय्यसहिष्णुः ।
भव समचित्तः सर्वत्र त्वं
वाञ्छस्यचिराद्यदि विष्णुत्वम् ॥ २४॥
units.translation: The one Viṣṇu is in you, in me, and elsewhere. You are intolerant and grow angry with me in vain. Be even-minded everywhere if you wish soon to attain the state of Viṣṇu.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
tvayi mayi cānyatraiko viṣṇu-
rvyarthaṃ kupyasi mayyasahiṣṇuḥ |
bhava samacittaḥ sarvatra tvaṃ
vāñchasyacirādyadi viṣṇutvam || 24||

units.label: Verse 25
units.deva:
शत्रौ मित्रे पुत्रे बन्धौ
मा कुरु यत्नं विग्रहसन्धौ ।
सर्वस्मिन्नपि पश्यात्मानं
सर्वत्रोत्सृज भेदाज्ञानम् ॥ २५॥
units.translation: Make no effort for conflict or reconciliation with enemy, friend, son, or relative. See the Self in everything and everywhere give up the ignorance that sees difference.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
śatrau mitre putre bandhau
mā kuru yatnaṃ vigrahasandhau |
sarvasminnapi paśyātmānaṃ
sarvatrotsṛja bhedājñānam || 25||

units.label: Verse 26
units.deva:
कामं क्रोधं लोभं मोहं
त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मानं भावय कोऽहम् ।
आत्मज्ञानविहीना मूढा-
स्ते पच्यन्ते नरकनिगूढाः ॥ २६॥
units.translation: Give up desire, anger, greed, and delusion; contemplate the Self by asking, “Who am I?” Fools deprived of Self-knowledge are tormented, sunk in hell.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
kāmaṃ krodhaṃ lobhaṃ mohaṃ
tyaktvā’’tmānaṃ bhāvaya ko’ham |
ātmajñānavihīnā mūḍhā-
ste pacyante narakanigūḍhāḥ || 26||

units.label: Verse 27
units.deva:
गेयं गीतानामसहस्रं
ध्येयं श्रीपतिरूपमजस्रम् ।
नेयं सज्जनसङ्गे चित्तं
देयं दीनजनाय च वित्तम् ॥ २७॥
units.translation: Sing the Gītā and the thousand names; constantly contemplate the form of the Lord of Śrī. Lead the mind into the company of the good, and give wealth to the poor.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
geyaṃ gītānāmasahasraṃ
dhyeyaṃ śrīpatirūpamajasram |
neyaṃ sajjanasaṅge cittaṃ
deyaṃ dīnajanāya ca vittam || 27||

units.label: Verse 28
units.deva:
सुखतः क्रियते रामाभोगः
पश्चाद्धन्त शरीरे रोगः ।
यद्यपि लोके मरणं शरणं
तदपि न मुञ्चति पापाचरणम् ॥ २८॥
units.translation: For pleasure, one engages in sexual enjoyment; afterward, alas, disease comes to the body. Although death is the final end in this world, one still does not give up sinful conduct.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
sukhataḥ kriyate rāmābhogaḥ
paścāddhanta śarīre rogaḥ |
yadyapi loke maraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ
tadapi na muñcati pāpācaraṇam || 28||

units.label: Verse 29
units.deva:
अर्थमनर्थं भावय नित्यं
नास्तिततः सुखलेशः सत्यम् ।
पुत्रादपि धनभाजां भीतिः
सर्वत्रैषा विहिता रीतिः ॥ २९॥
units.translation: Reflect always that wealth is misfortune; truly, there is not the slightest happiness from it. The wealthy fear even their sons; this pattern is seen everywhere.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
arthamanarthaṃ bhāvaya nityaṃ
nāstitataḥ sukhaleśaḥ satyam |
putrādapi dhanabhājāṃ bhītiḥ
sarvatraiṣā vihitā rītiḥ || 29||

units.label: Verse 30
units.deva:
प्राणायामं प्रत्याहारं
नित्यानित्य विवेकविचारम् ।
जाप्यसमेतसमाधिविधानं
कुर्ववधानं महदवधानम् ॥ ३०॥
units.translation: Practice breath control, withdrawal of the senses, and inquiry that distinguishes the eternal from the non-eternal. Practice samādhi together with mantra recitation; do this attentively—very attentively.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
prāṇāyāmaṃ pratyāhāraṃ
nityānitya vivekavicāram |
jāpyasametasamādhividhānaṃ
kurvavadhānaṃ mahadavadhānam || 30||

units.label: Verse 31
units.deva:
गुरुचरणाम्बुजनिर्भरभक्तः
संसारादचिराद्भव मुक्तः ।
सेन्द्रियमानसनियमादेवं
द्रक्ष्यसि निजहृदयस्थं देवम् ॥ ३१॥
units.translation: With deep devotion to the lotus feet of the guru, be free from worldly existence before long. Through such discipline of the senses and mind, you will see the Lord dwelling in your own heart.
units.sectionTitle: Verses 21–31 · Saṃsāra, seeing the Self in all, and devotion to Govinda
units.iast:
gurucaraṇāmbujanirbharabhaktaḥ
saṃsārādacirādbhava muktaḥ |
sendriyamānasaniyamādevaṃ
drakṣyasi nijahṛdayasthaṃ devam || 31||
